notes: Company background: mid-enterprise e-commerce platform operating multi-brand catalogs across NA and EU. Heavy seasonal variance (peak: Black Friday/Cyber Monday). Currently using homegrown search + Elastic for faceted search; evaluating semantic layer for catalog relevance and long-tail queries.
Primary pain: poor relevance for synonyms and attribute-ambiguous queries, conversion drop on mobile; current rerankers add latency and cost - want lower cost per query at scale.
Scale: ~8M active SKUs across brands, ~2.5TB product metadata (images + text). Indexing cadence daily with hourly deltas; peak query load estimated 30k QPS during peak campaigns (10x baseline).
Latency targets: p50 < 50ms for retrieval+rank, p95 < 200ms for end-to-end search response; willing to accept slightly higher p95 for long tail if core flows stay sub-150ms.
Cost target: aim to reduce end-to-end inference cost per query below $0.003 for average search (retrieval+rerank budgets combined). Strong focus on unit economics for catalog scale.

Architecture preference: bi-encoder for embedding-based retrieval (approximate ANN), then lightweight cross-encoder reranker for top-15 candidates. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for quantization + batching to meet cost target.
Routing/fallback: need policy for model fallback during bursts (cheaper model variant for non-converting queries) and regional routing (EU customers must hit EU-resident infra).

Security/compliance: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML for internal users, KMS integration for key management, audit logs retained 12 months. Data residency: product data and user session logs for EU storefronts must remain in EU region.

POC goals: ingest 2M representative SKUs, offline recall >= 92% on internal benchmark, reranker improves MRR by >= 7% vs baseline, cost per query simulated under 0.003 at 3x baseline load. POC length: 8 weeks.
Recent activity timeline: see timeline entries.
Quotes from call: 'We need search that scales up for BFCM without bankrupting growth.' — Head of Search.

use_case_summary: Workload: high-volume catalog semantic search + product reranking for e-commerce storefronts and marketplace listings.
Retrieval: embeddings for approximate nearest neighbor search across product text + attribute vectors; nightly full reindex and hourly deltas.
Reranking: cross-encoder candidate re-ranking with feature fusion (click-through, price match, personalization signal). Need deterministic fallbacks for unavailable model tier.
Traffic pattern: baseline steady QPS ~3k, campaign peaks up to 30k QPS for 48-72h windows. Desire burst autoscaling + predictable billing for burst capacity.
Quality metrics: prioritize recall@50 and MRR; also monitor business KPIs (CR, AOV) during A/B tests.
Operational needs: observability by route/model, token-level cost breakdown, quick rollback for model regressions, canary deploys for rerankers.
poc_plan: Week 0: SOW sign + dataset scoping. Provide sample of 2M SKUs (text + attributes + canonical images references).
Week 1-2: Ingest and build ANN index; baseline retrieval experiments (recall/latency).
Week 3-4: Train/validate cross-encoder reranker on in-house eval sets; offline MRR comparison vs baseline.
Week 5: Simulated load test to validate cost-per-query at 3x and 10x baseline; tune batching and model variants.
Week 6-8: Live A/B on subset of traffic (mobile + desktop) during non-peak window; collect business metrics and finalize runbook for BFCM.
Deliverables: performance report (latency/cost/recall), Redwood Optimize recipe with quantization and batching settings, recommended Dedicated vs Private topology for production.
commercial_notes: Initial commercial ask: committed burst capacity for 3 months around BFCM, flexible overage model. Customer prefers month-to-month trial for Dedicated before committing to annual reserved capacity.
Estimated ARR models requested: flat commit with burst credits vs usage-based billing with cap. Procurement asked for 90-day POC pricing and enterprise add-on for extended logging retention.
Next commercial step: AE to deliver two pricing scenarios and a short-term burst addendum.
